lecturas.texto: Most software documentation follows a similar structure: an overview, installation steps, and a list of examples. When you read documentation for a new library, it helps to skip straight to the examples first. You can understand what the tool does before you worry about every detail.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the text suggest doing first when reading new documentation?
opciones: Going straight to the examples
Memorizing the installation steps
Reading every detail in order
Ignoring the overview completely

Hire a new team member

opciones: Reach out to the client to confirm requirements

lecturas.texto: The project I'm working on classifies customer support tickets by urgency, so the team can respond to critical issues first. It uses a model trained on past tickets that were already labeled by support agents. So far, it's been fairly accurate, but we're still reviewing edge cases where the model gets confused.

preguntas.pregunta: What is the main purpose of the project described?
opciones: To classify support tickets by urgency so critical ones get answered first
To replace all support agents with a chatbot
To delete old support tickets automatically
To translate support tickets into other languages

preguntas.pregunta: What is the team still working on?
opciones: Reviewing edge cases where the model gets confused
Hiring more support agents
Deleting the training data
Changing the project's main goal

lecturas.texto: When an interviewer asks you to describe a time you disagreed with a teammate, they're usually less interested in who was right and more interested in how you handled it. A strong answer explains the disagreement briefly, focuses on how you worked toward a solution, and mentions what you'd do differently next time, if anything.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, what are interviewers usually most interested in when asking about a disagreement?
opciones: How the candidate handled the disagreement, not who was right
Proving that the candidate was always right
Whether the candidate avoids all disagreements
The exact date the disagreement happened

preguntas.pregunta: What should a strong answer mention, according to the text?
opciones: What the candidate would do differently next time, if anything
Only a detailed description of who was wrong
A list of every disagreement the candidate has ever had
Why the teammate was difficult to work with

lecturas.texto: Every morning at nine, the team spends ten minutes on a quick standup call. Each person says what they finished yesterday, what they plan to do today, and whether anything is blocking them. It's short on purpose, so longer discussions move to a separate conversation afterward.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is the standup call kept short, according to the text?
opciones: On purpose, so longer talks happen separately
Because nobody has anything to say
Because the team only meets once a week
Because managers are not allowed to join

lecturas.texto: Mateo had been stuck on the same bug for almost an hour. Instead of continuing to guess, he messaged a teammate and asked if she had a few minutes to take a look. She found the mistake in less than five minutes, and Mateo thanked her and made a note to ask for help sooner next time.

preguntas.pregunta: What did Mateo decide to do differently next time?
opciones: Ask for help sooner
Stop using that teammate's help
Never ask for help again
Wait even longer before asking

lecturas.texto: Good comments explain why a piece of code exists, not just what it does. If the code itself is clear, repeating it in a comment adds little value. But if there's a non-obvious reason behind a decision, like working around a bug in another system, that reason is worth writing down so the next person doesn't remove it by accident.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, when is a comment most worth writing?
opciones: When there's a non-obvious reason behind a decision
Whenever the code is already very clear
Only at the very start of a file
Never, because comments always add value

preguntas.pregunta: What risk does the text mention about missing comments?
opciones: The next person might remove something important by accident
The code will stop compiling
The file will become too short
The team will have to rewrite the whole project

lecturas.tema: Dar feedback en un code review
lecturas.texto: When leaving comments on someone else's code, it helps to be specific and to explain the reasoning, not just the preference. Saying 'this could cause a bug if the list is empty' is more useful than saying 'I don't like this.' It also helps to mention what's working well, not only what needs to change.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is 'this could cause a bug if the list is empty' considered more useful than 'I don't like this'?
opciones: It's specific and explains the reasoning
It's shorter to type
It avoids mentioning any code at all
It only focuses on personal preference

lecturas.tema: Explicar un bloqueo en un proyecto
lecturas.texto: When Sofia reported that her task was blocked, she didn't just say 'I'm stuck.' She explained exactly what she needed, who could unblock her, and what she had already tried. That level of detail meant her manager could act on it immediately instead of asking several follow-up questions first.

preguntas.pregunta: What made Sofia's report about being blocked especially useful?
opciones: It included exactly what she needed and who could help
It was written in very few words
It avoided mentioning what she had already tried
It was sent directly to the whole company

preguntas.pregunta: What was the result of Sofia's detailed report?
opciones: Her manager could act on it immediately
Her manager ignored the message
The project was cancelled
She had to repeat the report three times

lecturas.texto: During sprint planning, the team doesn't just list tasks; they discuss how confident they are about each estimate. A task that sounds simple but depends on an external team is treated differently from one the team fully controls, even if both are estimated at the same number of hours.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, why might two tasks with the same hour estimate be treated differently?
opciones: One depends on an external team and the other doesn't
One of them was written in a different language
Only one of them has a deadline
The team always treats every task exactly the same way

lecturas.tema: Pros y contras de una herramienta
lecturas.texto: Before adopting a new tool, the team listed what they liked about it, what concerned them, and what they would need to test before relying on it in production. The tool was faster than their current one, but it was also newer and had less community support, which made the team decide to try it on a small project first.

preguntas.pregunta: Why did the team decide to try the new tool on a small project first?
opciones: Because it was newer and had less community support
Because it was more expensive than the old tool
Because the old tool had completely stopped working
Because the whole team disliked the new tool

During the real demo, one button didn't work as expected, but because he had practiced, he knew how to continue without panicking.
